image_description: A close-up view of a motorcycle rear wheel assembly featuring a drilled disc brake rotor, a silver caliper with a red bleed screw cap, and wire spokes. The image focuses on the mechanical components against a blurred background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Circular metal rotor (disc), notably larger in diameter than its thickness.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor is clearly circular and thin relative to its diameter, consistent with a disc brake.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast metal mounted over rotor edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A metallic caliper assembly is visible straddling the outer edge of the rotor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is mounted to wheel hub with visible lug bolt pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a motorcycle wheel; it uses a central axle/sprocket carrier mounting system, not a car-style 'lug bolt pattern' which is part of the taxonomy definition but not applicable here. The mounting hardware is obscured by the sprocket carrier.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is ventilated (two plates with cooling fins) or solid.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor appears to be a single solid plate with drill holes, which fits the 'solid' criteria of the checkpoint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brake pads are rectangular friction material blocks pressing against rotor faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dark friction material of the brake pads is visible inside the caliper jaws, contacting the rotor.
A black hydraulic hose is visible entering the top of the caliper assembly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows machined concentric grooves or cross-drilled holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface clearly features a pattern of cross-drilled holes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface exhibits heat discoloration (blue/brown tint) from use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface is uniformly silver/metallic with no visible blueing or browning indicative of heat stress.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast aluminum or iron.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The caliper exhibits the texture and sheen of cast metal (likely aluminum alloy).

artifact_observations.reasoning: There is text embossed on the caliper ('BREMBO' style), but the characters are slightly malformed and lack sharp definition, typical of AI generation struggling with small industrial text.
Several wire spokes appear to merge into the rim or fade out without a clear nipple/connection point, lacking the distinct mechanical termination seen in real wheels.
The yellow background element has a smeared, painterly texture that lacks specific object definition, though it is out of focus.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of braking system and distinguish it from similar mechanical assemblies.
To verify the connectivity of the thin spokes to the rim and detect any fusion or floating artifacts.
To ensure the caliper sits correctly over the rotor in 3D space and does not melt into the background or wheel.
To analyze the legibility and correctness of the text on the caliper body.

focus_areas: Connectivity of wire spokes to the rim
Legibility of text on the caliper
Physical separation between caliper and rotor
Consistency of drill hole patterns on the rotor
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the spoke nipples where they meet the rim; AI often fails to render these small distinct parts. Also, verify if the 'Brembo' text is actual readable text or just glyph-like shapes. Check if the red cap on the caliper is structurally attached or floating.
